test.title: An event you helped to organise

document.cue: Describe an event you helped to organise.

text: I'd like to talk about a charity book fair that I helped to organise at my university last April. The idea was to collect second-hand books from students and staff, sell them cheaply, and give all the money to a local animal shelter that was struggling to pay for food and medicine.

It took place in the main hall on a Saturday, and there were six of us in the organising team. We spent about a month preparing: collecting boxes of books from every faculty, sorting them by subject, and persuading a few local cafés to donate coffee and pastries so that people would stay longer.

My job was publicity. I designed posters, ran a small social media page and recorded a short video with a couple of dogs from the shelter, which turned out to be the most successful part of the whole campaign. On the day itself, I was also on the cash desk, and at one point the queue went all the way to the door.

By the end of the afternoon we'd sold more than eight hundred books and raised about four hundred thousand tenge, which was twice our target. I was exhausted, but incredibly proud, especially when the shelter sent us photos of what they'd bought with the money.
It taught me that a small team with a clear plan can achieve far more than you'd expect.

tips.en: My job was publicity answers the bullet point clearly.
tips.kk: My job was publicity — «не істедіңіз» тармағына анық жауап.

tips.en: Twice our target makes the success convincing.

tips.ru: Twice our target — число делает успех убедительным.
